lessons.title: Inspecting for non-conformances on site
lessons.html:
Looking with a trained eye

In this work experience module you carry out planned inspections to find non-conformances and then solve the problems you find, under a mentor. A non-conformance is anything that does not meet the law, the abattoir's procedures, customer specifications or safety requirements.

Planning an inspection

  1. Choose the area and purpose: for example the dressing floor during production, or the chillers before dispatch.
  2. Prepare a checklist based on the procedures and the regulations under the Meat Safety Act 40 of 2000.
  3. Choose the time: some inspections during production, some before start-up, some unannounced.
  4. Wear the right protective clothing and follow hygiene rules for the area.

What to look at

  • Structure: damaged floors, walls, doors; condensation; drainage.
  • Equipment: sterilisers, hand basins, guards, condition of rails and hooks.
  • Practices: hand washing, knife sterilising, carcass handling, animal handling.
  • Product: contamination, temperatures, marking and labelling, separation of passed and detained product.
  • Records: complete, current, signed, values within limits.
  • Safety: protective equipment, lock-out, wet floors, chemical storage.

Recording findings

For each finding write what, where, when and the requirement it breaks. Be specific: Chiller 2, 07:30: condensation dripping from cooling unit onto three beef sides, rail 4. Grade findings by seriousness: critical (immediate food safety or safety risk), major (system failure), minor (isolated lapse). Take immediate action on critical findings.

lessons.title: Solving the problems you find
lessons.html:
A structured problem-solving method

For each significant finding, work through these steps with the people responsible for the area.

  1. Contain: protect people and product now. For the condensation example: move affected sides, trim or treat according to the inspector's direction, and stop loading under the unit.
  2. Describe the problem: what is happening, how often, how big, since when.
  3. Find the root cause: use the five whys and check causes under people, method, machines, materials, animals, environment and measurement. Use data and observation, not assumptions.
  4. Choose actions: address the root cause; prefer actions that change the system.
  5. Implement: assign an owner and a deadline.
  6. Verify: check that the problem has stopped.
  7. Standardise: update SOPs, checklists and training.

Worked example

Finding: Repeated hair contamination on beef carcasses at the trim check (8 per 100 carcasses against a normal of 2).

Investigation: Observation shows the hide opening cuts are made from the outside in at one station. A new worker took over the station last week. The SOP is posted but only in English, and the worker is more comfortable in isiXhosa.

Root causes: training not completed before the worker started alone; SOP not in a language the worker understands well.

Actions: coach the worker on inside-out cutting; translate key SOP steps and add photos; add a training sign-off before any worker works alone on a critical station.

Verification: trim check over two weeks shows hair findings back to 2 per 100.

lessons.title: Reporting, follow-up and evidence
lessons.html:
Writing the non-conformance report

Use the abattoir's non-conformance or corrective action form. Include:

  • Reference number, date, area and who found it.
  • Description and evidence (readings, photos where allowed, record copies).
  • Seriousness grading.
  • Immediate containment action.
  • Root cause analysis.
  • Corrective and preventive actions, owners and deadlines.
  • Verification result and close-out date, signed.

Following up

Keep a register of all open non-conformances. Review it weekly. Chase overdue actions politely but firmly, and escalate to the manager if they remain open. A non-conformance register with many old open items is itself a finding at audit.

Communicating results

Share what was found and fixed with supervisors and teams. When workers see that reported problems are solved, they report more. Avoid blaming individuals publicly; focus on the system.

Evidence for your portfolio

  • Inspection checklists you completed.
  • At least one full non-conformance investigation from finding to verified close-out.
  • The non-conformance register showing your follow-up.
  • Mentor observation reports and sign-off.
  • Reflections on what you learned about problem solving.

Key points

  • Plan inspections with a checklist based on procedures and regulations.
  • Record findings specifically and grade them as critical, major or minor.
  • Contain first, then find the root cause using data and observation.
  • Prefer system changes and verify that actions worked.
  • Keep a non-conformance register and follow up overdue actions.
